clue.text: Felt ruthless, turning to block swimmer

indicators.note: turning says the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters form a block sitting inside the phrase Felt ruthless, so block signals a hidden run

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone who felt merciless decides to obstruct a swimmer in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'block swimmer' as the definition, which leaves no hidden-word signal; 'to block' is that signal and 'swimmer' alone defines. 'turning' reads ELTRUT, inside 'fELT RUThless', backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine reptile that spends its life in the sea is a fair example of a creature that swims.

clue.text: Tuft of hair missing in the middle; check quality

indicators.note: missing in the middle says the central letter of the tuft word drops out

parts.note: a tuft of hair tied on the crown of the head is a topknot
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A hairdresser notes a bald patch in a tuft while checking quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing in the middle' takes K, the fourth of seven letters, out of TOPKNOT to leave TOPNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, as in quality goods, it means first-rate, excellent, of the highest standard.

clue.text: Farm animal displays some memory

definitions.meaning: an uncastrated male sheep kept on a farm
random-access memory, the working store of a computer

explanation.surface: A clever beast on the farm shows it can remember things.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a male sheep and a computer's random-access memory.

clue.text: But this bird has two of one, and none of the other

definitions.text: But this bird has two of one, and none of the other

parts.words: But this bird has two of one, and none of the other
parts.note: split the breed name into its two halves: the bird has a pair of limbs to stand on but no antler-like growth

explanation.surface: A riddle about a bird that has two of one thing and none of another.
explanation.walkthrough: The breed name splits into LEG and HORN: a chicken has two legs and no horn at all, so the name half lies.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of domestic chicken, originally from Livorno in Italy, so it is literally a bird.

clue.text: I'm hurt, having to go in non-upholstered carriage

indicators.note: to go in places the cry inside the word for unpadded

parts.note: a seat with no padding or covering is bare
ouch is the cry of someone in pain

explanation.surface: A passenger complains of pain after riding in a carriage with hard, unpadded seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding hood, popular in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Translating, had found faults in novel

indicators.note: translating turns text into another form, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A translator found mistakes in a novel while rendering it into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh's 1934 novel, whose title comes from a line in T. S. Eliot's The Waste Land.

clue.text: Manage as admirer at heart to preserve Gaelic

indicators.note: to preserve means to hold safely inside, so the language goes within
at heart keeps only the inner part of the admirer word, losing its two ends

parts.note: an admirer is a lover
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: A supporter of the language takes charge in order to keep Gaelic alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' leaves OVE; 'as' is only a link, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or direct work is to run it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Cold leads to bad congestion we know all about it

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: bad suggests the word congestion is corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A cold brings on a nasty blocked nose; we are all too familiar with it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means people with expert knowledge of a subject, the ones who can say they are in the know.

clue.text: Nestling in valley, almost lapped in warmth ——— not hot, though

indicators.note: lapped in means wrapped inside, so the shortened valley goes within
not hot tells us to drop the letter H, the abbreviation for hot

parts.note: warmth is heat

indicators.note: almost means the valley word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: Something snug in a valley, wrapped in warmth, yet not actually hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves GLE and 'not hot' leaves EAT; the first 'in' and 'though' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestling is a chick too young to leave the nest, and a young golden bird of prey is one.

clue.text: Christmas double act is long over: him and me sore to be sacked

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: to be sacked suggests the words are thrown out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sore performer complains that the Christmas double act has run too long and both partners face the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: A British pantomime is a Christmas stage show; this costume is worn by two actors, front and back legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-person costume animal of a festive stage show is literally a double act at Christmas time.

clue.text: English rock, for Aussie, sounds seedy stuff

indicators.note: sounds says the pair of words is said out loud to give a different spelling

parts.note: Australians call an English person a Pom, and granite is a hard rock

explanation.surface: An Australian names an English stone, apparently something rather seedy.
explanation.walkthrough: POM is Australian slang for a Briton; POM GRANITE spoken sounds like the fruit's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit is packed with juicy seeds, so calling it seedy stuff is a playful literal description.

clue.text: Part of stand-up routine makes one retch

definitions.meaning: a joke told by a comedian
to heave or choke as if about to vomit

explanation.surface: A comedian's set is so bad it makes someone feel sick.
explanation.definitionFit: The same short word means a comic joke and a verb for choking or heaving.

clue.text: From distant office, drive away, then choose to come back in

indicators.note: in puts the reversed word inside the driving-out word

parts.note: to oust is to drive out or expel

indicators.note: to come back means the choosing word is read in reverse

parts.note: to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: Someone forced out of a remote branch later chooses to return to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote branch or station far from headquarters, such as a colonial trading post.

clue.text: Rent delivered here? Exactly

definitions.meaning: rent goes to the person who lets out the property, the landlord

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'letter' as one who lets a property: the landlord is where rent is delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Following instructions with complete precision is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: One supplying broadband in measured quantity ——— put in order

indicators.note: in puts the provider inside the measured amount

parts.note: a dose is a measured quantity of medicine
an ISP, internet service provider, supplies broadband

explanation.surface: An internet provider rations broadband in fixed amounts to keep things orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange or set things out in position is an older sense of the verb, as troops are arranged.

clue.text: What suffragettes endured: a Tom and Jerry cartoon?

definitions.meaning: the 1913 British law letting hunger-striking prisoners be released and re-arrested
a performance by a cat chasing a mouse, as in the animated series

explanation.walkthrough: The Prisoners (Temporary Discharge for Ill-Health) Act of 1913 was nicknamed for the way it toyed with suffragettes.
explanation.definitionFit: The popular name for a British statute, and also a literal description of a feline-rodent routine.

clue.text: One maybe pickled in pub — the first to leave, you mean?

indicators.note: in puts the pickled thing inside the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
an egg may be pickled, as on a pub counter

indicators.note: the first to picks out only the opening letter of leave

parts.note: Y is a text-message abbreviation for you

explanation.surface: A drunk in a pub is told to be first out, and is called mean for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One maybe pickled' is not a drunk but an egg, a pub-counter snack; 'the first to' takes only L from 'leave'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry and miserly, fit only for a pauper, which is what mean signifies here.

clue.text: Free with complaints about unattractive personality trait

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who complains freely about others has an unattractive character.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflated sense of one's own worth is pompous vanity, widely thought an unappealing quality.

clue.text: Played on the roof?

parts.note: the musical Fiddler on the Roof suggests a violin played up on the rooftop

explanation.walkthrough: The musical Fiddler on the Roof suggests what was done up there: a violin was played.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a violin is to bow the strings, the past tense matching played.

clue.text: One shaken and weary at length calling doctor in

indicators.note: in, after calling, puts the doctor inside the weary-and-length letters

parts.note: to tire is to weary
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone shaken and exhausted after a long time finally calls in a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambourine-like percussion instrument, played by being shaken or struck.

clue.text: A church has abandoned God, count on it!

indicators.note: has abandoned means the church letters leave the god's name

parts.note: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine

explanation.surface: A congregation has lost its faith, and you can rely on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires used for arithmetic, something you literally count on.

clue.text: Murmur about daughter's size measurement

indicators.note: about means wrapped around, so the murmur word surrounds the daughter

parts.note: a breath, as in a breath of scandal, is a faint murmur or whisper

explanation.surface: A whisper goes round about the daughter's dress size.
explanation.definitionFit: Width from side to side is one dimension by which an object's size is measured.

clue.text: Showing off: it needs activity to hold me back

indicators.note: to hold means to keep within, so the reversed word sits inside

parts.note: doing is activity, as in 'there's a lot of doing here'

indicators.note: back says the word me is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A show-off says the activity needs to keep them in the spotlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes EM; 'it needs' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonstrating a product or a piece of software to an audience is displaying its features.

clue.text: Function that's provided for new arrival

definitions.meaning: the cotangent, a trigonometric function, abbreviated
a baby's bed with high barred sides, ready for a newborn

explanation.definitionFit: The trigonometry abbreviation for cotangent is also a baby's bed.

clue.text: My aerosol —- it's used with devotion

parts.note: My Lord! is an exclamation of surprise, so My stands for Lord
an aerosol is a sprayer

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims over a spray can that they use devotedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation, as in 'My Lord!', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known Christian prayer, recited in worship, so it is used in acts of devotion.

clue.text: Go off course, and manifest boredom no end

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the boredom word is dropped

parts.note: to yawn is to show boredom

explanation.surface: A bored helmsman yawns endlessly and drifts off course.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or aircraft swinging off its heading about a vertical axis does this.

clue.text: I want peace, getting more revolutionary security equipment

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
red is the colour of revolution, so more revolutionary is redder

explanation.surface: A radical demanding quiet becomes more extreme about security gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that cuts confidential papers into strips protects sensitive information.

clue.text: Being dishevelled, depressions break through

indicators.note: break means burst into, so the depressions go inside

parts.note: by means through, as in 'by means of'
lows are weather depressions, areas of low pressure

explanation.surface: A scruffy figure as weather fronts break through.
explanation.walkthrough: Meteorological 'depressions' are lows; 'through' as in 'by way of' gives BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse, untidy and unkempt in appearance, especially of a person's look or hair.
